Initial program setup

This replaces occupancy categories with a learned motion model trained through probabilistic matching of anonymous enemy sightings. A spatial belief tracks unseen enemy mass, while mission routing and three-step collision checks jointly choose actions. Board-location hypotheses also support explicit terrain estimates.
Learning diagnostics report prequential forecast error against persistence. Both ablation flags are preserved. Performance improvements remain to be verified by evaluation.

Add a learned spatial movement model that distributes enemy occupancy across reachable destinations. Train its mixture of stationary, cardinal and diagonal motion using next-observation Brier gradients, while retaining the existing categorical learner as a smoothing component. Predictive updates freeze when learn=False.
Use stronger immediate collision costs and bounded waiting when waiting offers a substantially safer next step. Correct locked-door geometry so planned diagonal moves respect interaction and corner constraints. The predictive_planning=False path continues to use the fixed observation-based heuristic.
This is an untested candidate; improvement requires development evaluation, including escape outcomes and forecast errors against persistence.

Replace near-field category-only forecasts with topology-constrained anonymous occupancy flow. Learn movement probabilities from subsequent visible occupancy using a shared online gradient update, without matching enemy identities. Retain the existing categorical learner for peripheral forecasts and expose the new learned probabilities separately.
Propagate occupancy one additional step for planning. Penalize immediate moves that leave no low-risk continuation, and apply the same continuation check when considering waiting. Both predictive-learning and predictive-planning ablations remain supported.
Separately fix diagonal traversal through still-locked doors: possessing both keys permits cardinal interaction, but does not make a diagonal door immediately traversable.
These are proposed changes; improvement over the supplied development results requires evaluation.

Separates mapping, anonymous motion inference, forecast calibration, and navigation. Learns movement tendencies from probabilistic associations between consecutive observations, then forecasts occupancy for each candidate action. Planning combines route progress with immediate collision risk and future escape options, while correcting locked-door traversal. Predictive learning and predictive planning can be disabled independently. Performance improvements require evaluation.

Replaces the motion-kernel mixture with a learned spatial transition model fitted directly to anonymous occupancy forecasts. Its features capture geometry, proximity, approach direction, and probabilistic motion continuity without assigning enemy identities. Unobserved enemy beliefs propagate through the remembered map.
Planning combines exploration and pathfinding with two-step comparisons of movement, retreat, and waiting. Predictive parameters freeze when learning is disabled; disabling predictive planning switches navigation to the fixed observation-based risk heuristic. Diagnostics separately record predictive updates and pre-update errors against persistence. These are proposed improvements; no additional evaluation results are claimed.

Preserves the successful occupancy learner while adding terrain-aware, temporally conditioned probability estimates and learned anonymous motion statistics. A bounded occupancy field carries information about enemies outside the current view. Planning uses corrected door traversal, equal-cost diagonal steps, persistent exploration targets, and explicit comparisons between waiting and moving, including uncertainty and available retreat cells. Predictive updates freeze under learn=False; predictive_planning=False uses observation-based risk while preserving navigation. Diagnostics compare forecasts with persistence on subsequently observed cells. Performance improvements remain unverified.

Separates mapping, predictive learning, navigation, and action evaluation into explicit stages. Anonymous motion inference trains a geometry-aware transport model, while online calibration learns how much to trust transport versus local occupancy statistics. Planning uses persistent exploration targets, action-conditioned forecasts, and survival-conditioned escape estimates. Forecast diagnostics compare predictions with persistence using subsequent observations; predictive parameters freeze when requested. Performance improvements require evaluation.

This design retains observation-based mapping and goal-directed navigation, but replaces gradient-based occupancy learning with a Bayesian model of attempted motion. It learns from the likelihood of whole anonymous enemy sets, summing over feasible assignments and treating departures from view as censored observations. Blocked motion attempts explicitly contribute to staying in place.
A mass-conserving hidden occupancy model maintains the three-enemy population. The planner compares action-conditioned forecasts and short-horizon survival costs while pursuing keys, the door, and exploration frontiers. Predictive learning and predictive planning can be disabled independently. Diagnostics report pre-update Brier errors against persistence and fractional learning evidence. Performance improvements require evaluation; none are claimed here.

The examples motivate anonymous occupancy forecasts and explicit collision avoidance. This design replaces motion-mixture fitting and enemy matching with a growing regression tree that learns spatial corrections to a mass-conserving diffusion prior. Tree splits arise from observed forecast residuals, allowing the predictive representation to expand during an episode.
Planning combines key-route ordering, information-gain exploration, and three-step survival-aware dynamic programming. Immediate movement excludes occupied cells; future costs account for occupancy both before and after movement. Predictive learning and predictive planning remain independently switchable. Exported diagnostics compare prequential predictions with persistence and the uncorrected diffusion prior. This is an unevaluated candidate; improved performance requires measurement.

Learn anonymous enemy transport directly, including persistence, directional bias, and momentum inferred from probabilistic incoming motion. Train transport parameters on next-observation Brier error while retaining the residual tree for local calibration. Freeze parameter updates when learn=False; localization and motion-state inference continue.
Change future planning to estimate the cost of selecting the best available move after observing enemy occupancy. This replaces the predictive planner’s repeated pre-movement collision penalties with explicit alternative-action availability, while retaining immediate collision avoidance and the fixed-risk ablation.
These changes target forecast accuracy and unnecessary detours or waiting. Performance improvement remains unverified.

Learn a spatial enemy-transport model from the full overlap of successive observations. Normalize occupancy-loss gradients by usable labels, exclude terrain changes, and learn how much each occupancy category trusts transport versus the existing calibrated forecast. Record errors against persistence using previously issued predictions; learn=False freezes all predictive parameters.
Jointly improve planning by considering safe continuation cells when comparing movement and waiting. Keep the existing mapping, exploration, and fixed-risk ablation. Separately fix diagonal entry into locked doors, which cardinal interaction cannot open from that position. These are proposed improvements, without new evaluation results.

Reorganizes the agent around a cached, lazy occupancy predictor shared by learning, planning, and export. Each candidate action gets its own conditioned forecast; second-step forecasts propagate that branch’s occupancy and inferred motion. Online learning updates a spatial transition model from anonymous occupancy labels, while mapping and diagnostics continue during learning ablations. Door interactions are included in branch geometry. This proposal is unevaluated; performance gains require empirical verification.

Make continuation planning account for both collision risk and onward progress. The current continuation estimate can favor a safe cell that requires abandoning the route or repeatedly waiting. Evaluate the next legal action using its hazard and route regret, retain escape-option costs at intermediate targets, and remove continuation costs only at a known, unlocked exit. Preserve Dijkstra routing, frontier hysteresis, and waiting penalties. The disabled-prediction branch uses the same navigation logic with its fixed observation-based risk heuristic.
Replace incremental mixture-gradient updates with regularized cumulative least-squares mixing of the transport and calibration forecasts. This directly minimizes historical Brier loss for the two issued predictors within each occupancy bucket, while preserving the existing anonymous-motion learner. Predictive parameters remain frozen when learn=False. These are proposed improvements; no new evaluation results are claimed.

Preserve each anonymous source’s mutually exclusive possible destinations during prediction. The planner then conditions continuation risk on surviving the first action, combines pre-movement and post-movement hazards without double counting, and propagates expected incoming velocity into its second-step forecasts. Transition caching limits repeated computation. This targets a representation error in the existing lookahead; improvement requires evaluation and is not assumed.

Condition unseen occupancy on newly observed empty cells, preserving each anonymous source’s mutually exclusive destinations. This improves belief inference without changing predictive parameters when learning is frozen.
Price safe continuation beyond intermediate targets when selecting goals and frontiers and when evaluating immediate arrival. Only a verified terminal exit receives zero continuation cost. Nearby targets use the existing survival-conditioned transition model; distant targets use discounted risk estimates. Preserve Dijkstra routing, frontier hysteresis, waiting penalties, and the observation-based planning ablation. These are proposed improvements; their performance requires evaluation.

Condition each continuation forecast on its own destination and compute pre-move and post-move collision jointly within each enemy’s trajectory. This avoids double-counting correlated hazards and accounts for learned pursuit behavior during the second action. Cache transition geometry and kernels within each observation to limit computation. Train occupancy calibration on all subsequently observed forecast cells, increasing predictive evidence without using hidden information. Learning freezes and the fixed-risk planning ablation remain intact. Performance improvement requires evaluation.

Replace the second-step forecast’s fixed anchor with the actual continuation destination. After evaluating a first move, condition each anonymous enemy distribution on surviving at that destination. For each continuation, account for collision before enemy movement, then propagate surviving occupancy toward the continuation destination using the learned transition model.
Cache transition geometry within each decision to limit rollout cost. Keep exported first-step forecasts unconditional for scoring, preserve predictive-learning freezes, and retain the fixed-risk planning fallback. This targets avoidable deaths without adding predictive parameters; improvement requires development evaluation.

Replaces occupancy buckets with hierarchical Bayesian motion learning, anonymous transition matching, and spatial enemy beliefs. A three-step survival planner compares movement, waiting, and retreat while routing toward keys and informative viewpoints. Sparse contexts inherit shared evidence; predictive updates freeze when requested. Synthetic interface, ablation, and resource checks passed; improved maze performance remains unverified.

Learn the transport-versus-frequency forecast mixture separately for each occupancy context using delayed Brier-loss gradients. Store both forecasts before observing their outcomes, and freeze mixture updates when learn=False.
Replace the safety-only continuation minimum with a goal-aware second-action rollout. Each continuation pays movement, remaining route cost, and conditional collision risk while preserving categorical alternatives within each anonymous enemy source. This prevents an apparently safe retreat or wait from concealing poor progress. Fixed-risk planning remains available when predictive_planning=False. These are proposed improvements; their performance requires evaluation.

This program replaces motion-kernel mixtures with hierarchical Bayesian transition learning. It jointly considers possible anonymous enemy movements, including movements outside the observed area, and maintains hidden occupancy across the inferred board.
Navigation uses a four-step survival planner over multiple candidate destinations. Reaching a key or frontier switches to an escape-option calculation, so dangerous intermediate arrivals remain costly. Forecast diagnostics compare pre-update predictions with persistence. Both ablation switches are preserved. Performance improvements require evaluation; none are claimed here.

This program learns an anonymous probabilistic cellular automaton directly from occupancy observations, without assigning enemy identities. An inventory-aware navigation graph represents key collection and door opening explicitly. Three-step recourse planning accounts for future observations and continues evaluating danger after reaching intermediate targets; only verified exit states terminate continuation.
Forecast diagnostics compare issued predictions against persistence and the unlearned automaton. Predictive parameters freeze under `learn=False`, and `predictive_planning=False` preserves navigation while substituting observation-based risk. Improved performance remains to be established by evaluation.

This program maintains weighted hypotheses over complete three-enemy configurations across observations. Observation-conditioned proposals enforce both detected enemies and empty cells, while hierarchical motion distributions learn from resolved transitions. Planning uses survival-conditioned scenarios and anticipates evasive actions after the next observation. Board-boundary inference improves reconstruction and exploration. Predictive-learning and planning ablations remain separate, and prequential diagnostics compare forecasts with persistence and the untrained motion prior. Performance improvements remain to be evaluated.

Maintain weighted anonymous three-enemy configurations across observations, filtering against both occupied and empty visible cells. Compute forecasts by exact inclusion-exclusion within this bounded ensemble, preserving categorical dependence. A small recovery proposal prevents permanent particle depletion.
Condition the next planning decision on survival and sampled observable enemy configurations, excluding occupied moves before comparing alternatives. Preserve the learned motion hierarchy, frozen-learning behavior, fixed-risk planning ablation, and existing third-step approximation.
Synthetic checks passed for filtering consistency, occupancy aggregation, parameter freezing, and planner integration. Improvement in combined_score remains unmeasured.

The current agent uses four transition features, a 0.24 learning rate, 25% empirical calibration, and unconditional two-step risk. This version expands the transition model to ten features and learns a confidence-shrunk residual tree directly from delayed occupancy errors. Splits require repeated evidence, at least 48 examples, and sufficient loss reduction; residual corrections are bounded.
Planning uses survival-conditioned second-step forecasts, cached transition geometry, and immediate/future risk weights of 72/20. Predictive parameters freeze under learn=False; predictive_planning=False retains mapping and pathfinding with fixed observation-based risk. Diagnostics compare pre-outcome forecasts against persistence and the residual-free model. These are proposed improvements, not newly measured results.

Retain each visible enemy's categorical transition branches in the world model. Score each first action using the same action-conditioned forecast that will be exported, then condition its continuation on surviving that action. At the next decision, separate the probability that a destination is available from the risk of an enemy arriving after movement. Propagate branch-specific velocities, with transition caches local to each candidate action.
This addresses double-counting and inconsistent future motion in the current marginal rollout while preserving transport learning, residual-tree learning, mapping, and both ablations. Unobserved enemies retain an approximate background forecast; future action availability still uses the existing approximate expected-choice calculation. Performance improvement requires evaluation.

Use every unchanged traversable cell in consecutive observation overlap for occupancy learning and calibration. Add a label-normalized Brier gradient to the existing anonymous motion learner, with bounded AdaGrad updates; retain the union derivative and exclude changed terrain from residual supervision. Predictive updates remain frozen when learn=False.
When both keys are mapped, compare complete two-key routes, including the approach to a known door, instead of choosing the nearest key independently. This preserves observation-based risk and pathfinding when predictive_planning=False. These are proposed improvements; their performance requires evaluation.

Train on the full unchanged, traversable observation overlap, averaging the transport gradient before regularization and AdaGrad. Preserve anonymous occupancy derivatives, bounded weights, and frozen predictive updates.
Improve planning by accounting for dependence between future escape options: one visible enemy cannot occupy several alternative destinations simultaneously. Compute their joint availability from the existing categorical motion branches, retaining the approximation for hidden enemies. This should reduce unnecessary waiting and detours without weakening immediate collision avoidance. Performance improvement requires evaluation; no new results are claimed.

Replaces the parametric motion model and residual tree with an online hierarchical categorical predictor over movement, geometry, relative heading, and agent position. Anonymous association supplies fractional training examples while preserving uncertainty about velocity.
Planning searches survival-conditioned enemy distributions through three future decisions, with action-conditioned forecasts and explicit collision checks before and after enemy movement. This is designed to improve escape safety without discarding mapping or efficient exploration. Forecast diagnostics compare learned predictions with both a frozen prior and persistence; performance improvements require evaluation.

Retain separate enemy distributions after conditioning on first-step survival. For each possible onward move, combine immediate occupancy and subsequent enemy arrival within each distribution, avoiding the current double counting of correlated hazards. Recompute enemy motion toward the onward destination using simulated key collection and door opening.
Only verified exit arrival ends continuation planning. Keys, doors, and frontiers retain survival checks. Preserve Dijkstra routing, frontier hysteresis, waiting penalties, predictive-update freezing, and the fixed-risk planning ablation. This changes the predictive representation and its use in planning; performance improvement remains unmeasured.

Replace hidden-cell independence with a bounded mixture of anonymous categorical enemy clouds. Between observations, propagate each cloud through the learned motion model. At the next observation, enumerate possible anonymous assignments, condition on both occupied and empty observed cells, and retain weighted alternatives. Existing transport and residual learning then operate on forecasts derived from this persistent representation.
Planning conditions the same mixture on survival and computes joint occupancy patterns over alternative moves. This avoids treating one uncertain enemy as several independent obstacles. Mixture pruning and conditional-average continuation hazards remain approximations; improvement requires evaluation. Learning and planning ablations retain their existing behavior.

The current program combines reflected motion, AdaGrad updates, a residual tree, and three-step planning with shared future forecasts. Its marginal corrections can lose categorical consistency, and candidate actions do not receive matching continuation forecasts.
This replacement learns a normalized, action-conditioned transition model and represents visible and hidden enemies as three categorical sources. Each first action receives its own forecast, survival conditioning, continuation cache, and two-step calculation. Continuation availability is integrated over correlated occupancy masks instead of independent cell probabilities.
Learning uses survival-conditioned Brier gradients, a 0.18 AdaGrad rate, 0.003 regularization, and twelve motion/context features. Planning uses survival penalties of 180 and 85, retaining exploration, mapping, and both ablations. Exports report pre-update forecast and persistence errors separately. These changes target safer, more consistent decisions; performance improvement remains unmeasured.

Learn a separate blend of motion forecasts and empirical occupancy rates for each observable context using delayed Brier gradients. Store the issued forecast components so learning uses only subsequent reliable observations; learn=False freezes these updates.
Replace the fixed second-step escape action with observation-contingent recourse. Approximate joint enemy transitions with 64 deterministic quadrature hypotheses, condition whole configurations on survival, and group them by the anonymous occupancy observable next turn. Choose one recourse action per observation group, preserving uncertainty about enemy association. Export retains analytical marginal forecasts, avoiding sampling noise in scored predictions. The fixed-risk planning ablation remains intact. Performance improvement requires development evaluation.

Retain probabilistic occupancy when enemies leave view, condition it on subsequent observations, and propagate it with the learned transition kernel. Untracked enemy mass remains diffuse. This extends predictive state estimation without introducing identities or updating parameters when learning is disabled.
Use the retained occupancy in exported forecasts, route costs, and second-step collision estimates. Record separate forecast errors on newly revealed tracked cells against a diffuse-background counterfactual. This is an untested candidate; the supplied results do not establish its improvement.

Preserve enemy motion alternatives as categorical distributions instead of turning each possible destination into another independent enemy. Represent the remaining hidden enemies with normalized categorical distributions, and include their predicted arrivals in anonymous assignment learning instead of using the fixed unmatched-enemy penalty.
Replace second-step diffusion with source-wise recourse conditioned on surviving the first destination. This removes impossible occupied-at-the-survivor hypotheses and avoids charging entry and subsequent collision as independent events. Cache local transition probabilities across candidate actions. Mapping, pathfinding, predictive-update freezing, and the fixed-risk planning ablation remain intact.
This analytically integrates a factorized configuration model; it does not implement the recommended particle filter. The expected benefit is less unnecessary waiting while retaining immediate collision penalties. Performance improvement requires evaluation.

Add a confidence-shrunk residual tree to the existing ten-feature transition softmax. Grow contextual partitions from anonymous occupancy-loss gradients only after repeated split evidence, preserving normalized movement alternatives. Record pre-outcome errors against both the uncorrected softmax and persistence, including while learning is frozen.
Make planning evaluate each candidate action using its own conditioned enemy forecast and continuation cache. This aligns action selection with the forecast subsequently exported and learned. These are proposed improvements; their effect requires evaluation.

Uses the strongest supplied ancestor’s learned motion model and categorical two-step planning. Every candidate action receives its own forecast, survival-conditioned continuation, and separate transition cache. The selected forecast is reused unchanged for export and delayed learning. Mapping and forecast diagnostics continue when learning is frozen; predictive-planning ablation uses only fixed observation-based risk. Geometry caching limits repeated computation. Performance improvements require evaluation; no new results are claimed.

Replace the shared three-step marginal rollout with a two-step rollout for each candidate action. Learn action-conditioned enemy approach behavior alongside momentum, represent the three enemies as categorical sources, and condition continuation risk on surviving the first move and observing an empty second destination. Integrate future action availability using categorical occupancy masks instead of independent cell probabilities.
Save the exact first-action forecast used for selection for export and subsequent learning. Retain the residual tree for immediate forecast calibration; continuation uses the categorical transport model. Cache hidden-source transport within each observation to limit computation. Mapping and both ablations remain intact. This is a proposed improvement; no additional performance measurements are claimed.

Replaces sampled enemy configurations with deterministic occupancy transport and an online, censored-transition motion learner. An augmented navigation graph tracks key collection and door opening; observation-contingent reach-avoid planning continues beyond intermediate goals and terminates only at an unlocked exit. Forecast diagnostics compare issued predictions with persistence and the prior motion kernel. Learning and predictive-planning ablations remain supported. Performance improvements require evaluator confirmation.

Replace the second-step decision made before observing enemy motion with observation-conditioned recourse. Enumerate the small joint distribution induced by the learned transition kernels, condition on first-step survival, and group hypotheses by the anonymous enemy positions visible from the destination. Choose the safest continuation separately for each possible observation, averaging over ambiguous associations within that observation. This preserves unconditional forecasts for export and retains the diffuse approximation for unseen enemies.
Also train the transition features directly against occupancy Brier loss alongside association learning and the residual tree. Exclude changed terrain from this predictive update so wall changes do not become misleading motion labels. Existing learning and planning ablations remain intact. These are proposed improvements; no new performance measurements are claimed.

Train from unchanged traversable cells observed in consecutive frames, using saved forecasts and anonymous occupancy labels. Average gradients by the supervised cell count, separate prior shrinkage from AdaGrad, and normalize residual-tree evidence consistently. Preserve existing diagnostic coverage and expose the broader supervision count.
For planning, count entering an occupied cell as lethal and avoid double-counting subsequent motion from that same source. This should discourage dangerous second-step commitments while preserving observation-based planning under ablation. These are proposed improvements; their effect on escape rate requires evaluation.

Replaces sampled enemy configurations with persistent categorical distributions. Joint association prevents duplicate confirmation of sightings; hidden alternatives remain mutually exclusive within each source. Censored transition learning separates predictive parameters from filtering, preserving frozen-learning behavior.
Planning conditions entire source distributions on survival and evaluates observation-dependent continuation actions using their actual candidate destinations. Mapping, key ordering, exploration, and forecast-versus-persistence diagnostics remain intact. Performance improvement requires evaluation; no new benchmark results are claimed.

Use joint anonymous association to infer motion: competing explanations must respect observed empty cells and assign each previously visible source to at most one observed enemy. Hidden arrivals and departures beyond the observation remain possible. This improves the motion features consumed by the existing transport learner without introducing persistent identities; inference continues when learning is frozen.
Replace independent continuation-availability estimates with a categorical occupancy-mask calculation. A single enemy cannot simultaneously block several alternative moves. Integrating these mutually exclusive outcomes preserves survival conditioning, action-conditioned forecasts, the two-step horizon, and progress penalties. Hidden occupancy retains its existing approximation. These are proposed improvements; their effect on the combined score requires evaluation.

Retain three anonymous categorical enemy tracks across observation gaps. Joint maximum-likelihood association assigns each occupied observation to one track; visible empty cells remove incompatible locations. Each track includes an unlocalized probability mass, and bounded support compression transfers discarded mass there without renormalizing retained locations.
Forecast union occupancy from whole tracks, reduce ambient density by represented enemy mass, and condition entire tracks on survival during continuation planning. Hidden-track propagation is shared across candidate actions using the current agent position; visible enemies retain action-conditioned forecasts. Existing predictive learning remains active, with its occupancy gradients adjusted for hidden-track survival probabilities. Filtering continues when learn=False, while predictive_planning=False retains the existing observation-based planning path.
This is a proposed improvement, not a measured gain. Association uses a single best assignment rather than retaining uncertainty across assignments.

Simulate key collection and door interaction before evaluating continuation actions. This repairs second-step legality and enemy geometry while preserving unconditional forecasts for scoring. Continue planning through intermediate targets by selecting a successor objective and charging a small route-progress penalty alongside observation-conditioned danger. Only an exit reached with the door actually open receives terminal treatment.
Extend predictive calibration to all reliably observed, unchanged traversable cells, retaining near-cell diagnostics and respecting learn=False. This supplies more occupancy labels without treating terrain changes as enemy behavior. These are proposed improvements; their performance requires evaluation.

Combines action-conditioned forecasting with progress-aware, survival-conditioned lookahead. Adds anonymous motion association, Brier learning across overlapping observations, propagation of hidden motion, and joint ordering of known keys. Target arrival also considers subsequent safety. Both ablation switches remain supported, and diagnostics separate prediction errors from parameter updates. This candidate requires evaluation; no performance improvement is claimed yet.

Add a bounded contextual residual tree to the normalized enemy transition model. It learns from marginalized anonymous associations, shrinks corrections with limited evidence, and splits only after repeated evidence of different gradients across contexts. Preserve the existing baseline learner and freeze all predictive updates when learning is disabled. Exclude wall-change transitions from parameter updates while continuing localization and motion inference.
Change continuation planning to evaluate actions after observing possible enemy positions, and score compounded survival logarithmically. This preserves navigation while discouraging high-risk shortcuts. Export residual-learning diagnostics separately from mapping. These are proposed changes; improved performance requires evaluation.

Preserve separate categorical enemy distributions across observation gaps instead of merging hidden enemies into one shared distribution. Jointly assign visible enemies to prior sources using an injective maximum-likelihood association, then condition unmatched sources on all visible cells being empty. Association ambiguity is approximated by its most likely assignment; location uncertainty within each hidden source remains intact. A small spatial recovery mixture prevents impossible associations after terrain changes.
Propagate these separate distributions through the learned transition model and the existing survival-conditioned continuation planner. Also evaluate safe continuation when reaching keys and exploration targets; only a terminal exit ends lookahead. This addresses the current planner’s tendency to ignore escape routes immediately after reaching an intermediate target. Predictive parameter freezing and the fixed-risk planning ablation remain intact. Performance improvement requires evaluation.

Adds a learned, age-dependent terrain transition model using reobservation evidence. Routing accounts for expected blockage, exploration values stale-wall refreshes, and local planning rewards observations that clarify the intended route. Anonymous enemy filtering retains survival-conditioned planning while replacing sampled motion updates with posterior expected transition counts. Both predictive learners respect frozen-learning mode; the planning ablation uses fixed observation-based risk. Exports include separate motion and terrain prediction diagnostics against persistence. Performance improvements require evaluation; no new results are claimed.

Separates mapping, learning, forecasting, and navigation through explicit observation and forecast snapshots. Residual-tree updates aggregate gradients before changing parameters, avoiding transition-order dependence while preserving conservative, evidence-driven splitting. Planning retains anonymous observation-conditioned recourse and accounts for key collection, door interaction, and route progress in continuation decisions. Predictive-learning and predictive-planning ablations remain independent. Performance improvements require evaluation; no new benchmark results are claimed.
